answer: Neighborhood Closure Rule: an agent must hold one stable position in a small-world neighbor graph, and each new identity needs a distinct cluster of mutually non-adjacent introducers to close into that graph. A raven posing as many agents fragments into isolated pockets that normal peers refuse to route through. The zephyr of routine traffic never reaches the closure threshold, so fake nodes stay quarantined. At its zenith, the attacker must maintain many separate live neighborhoods with real edges, multiplying infrastructure and coordination cost per identity.
